questions.questionText: She _____ to school every day.
questions.explanation: Third-person singular "she" takes the singular verb form "goes" in present simple tense.

questions.questionText: I saw _____ elephant at the zoo.
questions.explanation: The word "elephant" begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article "an" is used.

questions.questionText: They _____ playing cricket now.
questions.explanation: Plural subject "they" requires the plural auxiliary verb "are" in present continuous tense.

questions.questionText: This is Rani. _____ is my friend.
questions.explanation: Rani is a female singular person, so the personal pronoun "She" is correct.

questions.questionText: We _____ dinner at 8 p.m. yesterday.
questions.explanation: The past time marker "yesterday" requires the past simple form "ate".

questions.questionText: The book is _____ the table.
questions.explanation: We use "on" for contact with a horizontal or vertical surface like a table.

questions.questionText: There _____ two apples in the basket.
questions.explanation: "Two apples" is plural, so the plural verb "are" is required in present tense.

questions.questionText: I _____ here since 2022, and I still live here.
questions.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing into the present requires present perfect ("have lived").

questions.questionText: If she _____ hard, she will pass the exam.
questions.explanation: In first conditional clauses (If + present simple, will + base verb), use "studies".

questions.questionText: She is interested _____ learning English.
questions.explanation: The adjective "interested" takes the preposition "in".

questions.questionText: By the time we arrived, the movie _____.
questions.explanation: Past perfect ("had started") indicates an action completed before another past event.

questions.questionText: Neither Ravi nor his friends _____ ready.
questions.explanation: In "neither... nor" constructions, the verb agrees with the closer subject ("his friends", plural).

questions.questionText: This is the woman _____ helped me yesterday.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun "who" refers to people acting as the subject of the clause.

questions.questionText: He was tired, _____ he continued working.
questions.explanation: "But" introduces a contrasting coordinating idea between two independent clauses.

questions.questionText: If I _____ about the traffic, I would have left earlier.
questions.explanation: Third conditional (unreal past) uses "had known" with "would have left".

questions.questionText: The manager said, "I am busy." Choose the correct reported speech form.
options: A) The manager said that I am busy.
B) The manager said that he was busy.
C) The manager said that he is busy yesterday.
D) The manager said that he were busy.
questions.correctAnswer: B) The manager said that he was busy.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, present simple shifts back to past simple ("am" -> "was").

questions.questionText: Choose the correct passive form: "They have completed the project."
options: A) The project has been completed.
D) The project has being completed.
questions.correctAnswer: A) The project has been completed.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive structure: has/have + been + past participle ("has been completed").

questions.questionText: No sooner _____ the station than the train left.
questions.explanation: Negative inversion after "No sooner" requires auxiliary verb before subject: "had we reached".

questions.questionText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: A) Despite of the rain, we went out.
B) Although the rain, we went out.
C) In spite of the rain, we went out.
D) Despite it was raining, we went out.
questions.correctAnswer: C) In spite of the rain, we went out.
questions.explanation: "In spite of" is followed by a noun phrase ("the rain"). "Despite" does not take "of".

questions.questionText: Choose the correct sentence using inversion for emphasis.
options: A) Rarely I have seen such a beautiful view.
B) Rarely have I seen such a beautiful view.
C) Rarely did I have seen such a beautiful view.
D) Rarely I saw have such a beautiful view.
questions.correctAnswer: B) Rarely have I seen such a beautiful view.
questions.explanation: When a sentence begins with a negative adverb like "Rarely", subject-auxiliary inversion is used ("have I seen").
